item.title: Weekly Newsletter #19 — April 3, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #19 · April 03, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

📚 LIFE AFTER CARS BOOK TALK

Get your tickets before they sell out!

Thursday, May 14 at 7 PM — Spend an evening with Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon, hosts of the War on Cars podcast and authors of Life After Cars. They'll discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can build safer, more livable streets in Philadelphia.

Get Your Ticket Today

📣 BECOME A BETTER ADVOCATE

🚋💨 FASTER TROLLEYS

We're excited to report that our trolleys are on track to get a lot faster!
Starting this past Wednesday, drivers who block trolleys will receive $51 fines thanks to bus- and trolley-mounted automated cameras.

🏙️ OPEN STREETS THIS WEEKEND

This Sunday, portions of Walnut and 18th Streets in the Rittenhouse area will be car-free from 10am to 5pm as part of Center City District's West Walnut Open Streets.

Enjoy the beautiful spring weather and see how great our city can be when our streets put people first.

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🌳 SHAPE OUR FUTURE TRAIL NETWORK

The City is working on a new Trail Master Plan and they're looking for your feedback! They want to know how you use trails and how you think the existing trail network can be improved. Take their survey here!

📅 EVENTS

Apr 09

Fully Funded CCP - Press Conference

1:00 PM – 3:00 PM ·  CCP Bonnell Courtyard, 1700 Spring Garden St

Join Transit Forward Philly as they rally with the Community College of Philadelphia Federation of Staff, Student and Community Leaders to support their fight for SEPTA passes.
Apr 15

SEPTA Annual Service Plan Open House & Public Hearing #1

11:00 AM – 1:00 PM · 1234 Market St, hearing virtual via Webex

In-person only open house at 11am, followed by a hybrid public hearing at 12pm as SEPTA prepares to roll out New Bus Network.
Apr 15

SEPTA Annual Service Plan Open House & Public Hearing #2

5:00 PM – 7:00 PM · 1234 Market St, hearing virtual via Webex

In-person only open house at 5pm, followed by a hybrid public hearing at 6pm.
Apr 20

The Big Dig Podcast Live

7:00 PM – 9:00 PM · Pen and Pencil, 1522 Latimer St

Every American city is divided by crumbling old highways. Every city is trying to figure out what to do with them. Join Ian Coss, host of the Peabody-Award winning podcast “The Big Dig” – along with special guests – for a live taping about Philadelphia’s own attempts to solve that puzzle, and undo the harms of the past.
May 14

Life After Cars Book Talk

7:00 PM, doors open 6:30 PM · Resurrection Philadelphia, 123 S. 17th St

Spend an evening with Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon, hosts of the War on Cars podcast and authors of Life After Cars. They'll discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can build safer, more livable streets in Philadelphia.

📖 WHAT WE'RE READING

🏙️ HOUSING & LAND USE

WHYY / A vacant factory on Broad Street may be adapted for affordable senior apartments

Inquirer.com / SEPTA seeks apartment development near its stations to boost ridership and revenue

🌳 PUBLIC SPACE

Inquirer.com / A year after 4,000 tires were found dumped, Tacony Park is much cleaner. And a new preserve awaits.

🚌 TRANSIT

fox29.com / Philadelphia to start $51 fines for double parking in trolley lanes April 1

Billy Penn at WHYY / SEPTA bus route revamp starts in August

PhillyVoice / SEPTA to begin shuttle bus service on the Norristown High Speed Line amid repairs

Billy Penn at WHYY / SEPTA to add 24 new Canadian cars to its lineup, thanks to state funding

🚲 MOBILITY

Billy Penn at WHYY / Mayor Parker proposes delivery tax to pay for “pothole squads”

Delco Times / Bicyclists ride to honor Swarthmore professor hit, killed on his bike

Inquirer.com / Improving safety on Philadelphia’s roads is just as important as preventing violent crime in its streets | Editorial

💼 JOB OPPORTUNITIES

The Kelsey / Senior Manager, Land Use and Building Code

TTF Watershed Partnership

  • Community Organizer
  • Delaware River Watershed Fellowship

TYLin City Solutions / Senior Transportation Planner

Strong Towns National Gathering / Scholarship

Glitter / Director of Operations

City of Philadelphia

Multimodal Community Coordinator

Senior Capital Projects Manager (Chinatown Stitch)

Manager, Vending Strategy and Programs

School Crossing Guard

 

Do You Like This Newsletter and Our Advocacy Work?

We need your support to sustain Philly's Urbanist Movement — and you get cool perks too.

Join Us as a Member TODAY

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #18 — March 26, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #18 · March 26, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🚏 WE WON REAL-TIME BUS SIGNS

SEPTA is FINALLY launching a pilot program to deploy digital real-time arrival displays at selected bus and trolley stops across the system.

Our advocates have been speaking in support of these signs for months at SEPTA board meetings, so we're thrilled to see that our advocacy worked.

Real-time bus information is a basic feature that should be available to everyone waiting for the bus, not just to those with smartphones.

Have ideas about where these signs should go first? SEPTA wants to hear them.

🕯️ SATURDAY: REMEMBERING TEDDY EINSTEIN

This Saturday, the Bicycle Coalition will be hosting a memorial ride and ghost bike dedication for Teddy Einstein, a beloved husband and father of two young children who was killed by a driver while biking on Baltimore Pike.

Groups of cyclists will meet up at 9:45am in West Philadelphia (43rd and Chester) and Swarthmore (Myers and Park Avenue, Swarthmore Train Station) to bike to the scene of the crash at 10am.

There will be a pop-up intersection reconfiguration to demonstrate a safer intersection. At 11am there will be a brief ghost bike dedication ceremony, followed by cyclists biking back to West Philly and Swarthmore.

🏫 SUPPORT BETTER STUDENT TRANSIT ACCESS

We're working with Transit Forward Philadelphia to push for universal student fares and want to hear from students, teachers and family members--share your support for universal student fares here.

👋 WE'RE HIRING! - LAST CHANCE TO APPLY

We're excited to announce that we're hiring a part-time Executive Director! Applications submitted by April 1st will be prioritized.

The Executive Director (ED) serves as the chief executive and strategic leader of 5th Square Advocacy. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the ED is responsible for advancing the organization's mission through strong leadership, financial stewardship, partnership development, and operational excellence.

Know someone who'd be a great fit? Share this opportunity — we're looking for a passionate urbanist leader ready to take on Philadelphia's most important transportation and housing fights.

Apply Here

item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #17 · March 20, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🏫 UNIVERSAL STUDENT FARES

We're working with Transit Forward Philadelphia to push for universal student fares and want to hear from students, teachers and family members--share your support for universal student fares here.

Current student fare cards don't do enough to meet the needs of Philadelphia students.

While the School District of Philadelphia incentivizes parents to drive their kids to school with generous subsidies, we think we can do more for students who take SEPTA.

🌳 SHAPE OUR FUTURE TRAIL NETWORK

The City is working on a new Trail Master Plan and they're looking for your feedback! They want to know how you use trails and how you think the existing trail network can be improved.

Take their survey here!

They're also hiring Trail Ambassadors--apply here!

Ambassadors will receive a $600 stipend and will have the chance to influence priorities, messaging, and recommendations in the Trail Master Plan.

🏙️ MORE OPEN STREETS

Center City District's West Walnut Open Streets are coming back!

On Sundays from April 5th to May 17th, portions of Walnut and 18th Streets in the Rittenhouse area will be car-free from 10am to 5pm.

🚲 TOMORROW: POP-UP PROTECTED BIKE LANE

More than a year and a half after Dr. Barbara Friedes was tragically killed by a drunk driver while biking in the Spruce Street bike lane, there is still no concrete protection.

Join Philly Bike Action tomorrow on March 21st at 9am for a demonstration to show how concrete protected bike lanes would look and function on Spruce and Pine Streets. Coffee and donuts will be provided.

This is in addition with an increase in the City's contribution to SEPTA operating and capital funding.

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #15 — March 5, 2026
item.description:
👋 WE'RE HIRING!

We're excited to announce that we're hiring a part-time Executive Director!

The Executive Director (ED) serves as the chief executive and strategic leader of 5th Square Advocacy. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the ED is responsible for advancing the organization’s mission through strong leadership, financial stewardship, partnership development, and operational excellence. This is a hands-on, high-impact position in a lean, traditionally all-volunteer, organization.

Apply here.

📚 LIFE AFTER CARS BOOK TALK

Announcing our Life After Cars Book Talk!
Thursday, May 14 at 7 PM
Pre-sale opens TODAY to members of 5th Square Advocacy -- Sign up here to become a member and score your ticket!
Spend an evening with Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon, hosts of the War on Cars podcasts and authors of Life After Cars. The event will be kicked off by Councilmember Jamie Gauthier and emceed by the Inquirer's Inga Saffron.
The authors will discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can create safer, more liveable streets in Philadelphia.

💳 TOMORROW: RALLY TO SAVE ZERO FARE

Tomorrow at 10am outside City Hall, rally to save the Zero Fare program!

The next city budget may cut the hugely successful Zero Fare program and SEPTA Key Advantage for City employees.

Our advocates fought hard for these two programs which together provide reduced-fare or fare-free SEPTA access for over 70,000 Philadelphians--don't let them get cut!

Sign Transit Forward Philadelphia's petition calling on the City to keep these vital programs and join their rally this Friday.

🔥 FIRESIDE CHAT RECAP

Thanks for coming to our fireside chat last week!

We had a great discussion with Angela Brooks focusing on Mayor Parker’s HOME initiative and how pro-housing advocates can get involved in Philly's housing movement.

 

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. Should you have to choose which organization to support with your membership, we highly recommend choosing 5th Square Advocacy.

📰 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

Grid Magazine / The efforts to eradicate traffic deaths in Philadelphia launched in 2016. Ten years in, the City is still far from its goal

Not all of Vision Zero’s barriers emerge from Harrisburg. Many are a symptom of dysfunction right here in Philadelphia, says Will Tung, an organizer with the urbanist group 5th Square Advocacy.

“We’re kind of beholden to the roadway paving schedule here,” he says. “OTIS very much ties Vision Zero improvements with the paving schedule, mostly for budgetary reasons. They don’t want to implement a roadway change and then have it get ripped out for repaving a year or two later.”

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🗳️ Run for Committee Person

Running for committee person is surprisingly easy and impactful! Our sister-org 5th Square PAC is encouraging you to run and is providing a tool kit to help you get elected. Sign up here to receive a toolkit of voter lists, how-to guides, and petition forms.

🚏 Intercity Bus Terminal Survey

👋 WE'RE HIRING!

We're excited to announce that we're hiring a part-time Executive Director!

The Executive Director (ED) serves as the chief executive and strategic leader of 5th Square Advocacy. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the ED is responsible for advancing the organization’s mission through strong leadership, financial stewardship, partnership development, and operational excellence. This is a hands-on, high-impact position in a lean, traditionally all-volunteer, organization.

Apply here.

📚 LIFE AFTER CARS BOOK TALK

Announcing our Life After Cars Book Talk!
Thursday, May 14 at 7 PM
Pre-sale opens TODAY to members of 5th Square Advocacy -- Sign up here to become a member and score your ticket!
Spend an evening with Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon, hosts of the War on Cars podcasts and authors of Life After Cars. The event will be kicked off by Councilmember Jamie Gauthier and emceed by the Inquirer's Inga Saffron.
The authors will discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can create safer, more liveable streets in Philadelphia.

💳 TOMORROW: RALLY TO SAVE ZERO FARE

Tomorrow at 10am outside City Hall, rally to save the Zero Fare program!

The next city budget may cut the hugely successful Zero Fare program and SEPTA Key Advantage for City employees.

Our advocates fought hard for these two programs which together provide reduced-fare or fare-free SEPTA access for over 70,000 Philadelphians--don't let them get cut!

Sign Transit Forward Philadelphia's petition calling on the City to keep these vital programs and join their rally this Friday.

🔥 FIRESIDE CHAT RECAP

Thanks for coming to our fireside chat last week!

We had a great discussion with Angela Brooks focusing on Mayor Parker’s HOME initiative and how pro-housing advocates can get involved in Philly's housing movement.

 

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. Should you have to choose which organization to support with your membership, we highly recommend choosing 5th Square Advocacy.

📰 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

Grid Magazine / The efforts to eradicate traffic deaths in Philadelphia launched in 2016. Ten years in, the City is still far from its goal

Not all of Vision Zero’s barriers emerge from Harrisburg. Many are a symptom of dysfunction right here in Philadelphia, says Will Tung, an organizer with the urbanist group 5th Square Advocacy.

“We’re kind of beholden to the roadway paving schedule here,” he says. “OTIS very much ties Vision Zero improvements with the paving schedule, mostly for budgetary reasons. They don’t want to implement a roadway change and then have it get ripped out for repaving a year or two later.”
